title: Decide the PC price and what stays free on the web
statusNote: No PC price is set, and the full game is free on the web build, the single-file HTML and the phone apps.
steps: Pick one base price for all PC stores; $3.99 fits the $2.99-$4.99 band of Steam sudoku games.
Decide if the web version stays full and free, becomes a demo (e.g. Sector 1 + Daily), or goes offline.
Decide if you want Steam achievements (it makes Epic achievements mandatory too).
Decide if you want a free, ad-funded web version on portals at all.
Write the decisions into docs/STORE_CHECKLIST.md so every store page matches.
feedback: A complete free web game undercuts a paid PC version; sell the PC edition as complete and ad-free.
Steam launch discounts max out at 40%, then no discounts for 30 days.
Free-to-play on PC can't recoup Steam's $100 fee: there are no PC ads or purchases.
doneMessage: Price and free/paid split are settled, so every store page can be filled in the same way.

title: Verify space photo licenses and add a credits screen
statusNote: The 6 photos in game/public/space came with the prototype, sources are unknown, and the game has no credits or licenses screen.
steps: Trace each image in public/space to its source page (reverse image search).
NASA-made: public domain. ESA/Webb or ESA/Hubble: CC BY 4.0, visible credit required.
Replace any image you can't trace or license.
Add Settings > Credits: photo credits, fonts, 'made with AI assistance'.
Ship the SIL OFL license text with the fonts (e.g. a licenses/ folder in every build).
feedback: Every store agreement and Steam's content survey make you confirm you own or license all content.
Copy the ESA credit line exactly; don't use NASA/ESA logos or imply endorsement.
This applies to all PC stores, the web build and the phone apps.
doneMessage: Your content is safe to sell anywhere, removing the biggest legal risk.

title: Publish a site: privacy, support, press and play
statusNote: docs/PRIVACY.md is an unfilled template and nothing is hosted publicly yet.
steps: Fill in docs/PRIVACY.md (your name, contact email); keep 'desktop and web send no data'.
Pick a host: Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or GitHub Pages (free only for public repos).
Serve from a domain root you control (custom domain or <user>.github.io), not a sub-path.
Publish /privacy, a support email, /press and /play (web build or demo).
Add /app-ads.txt at the root once AdMob gives you the line (for the phone apps).
feedback: AdMob reads app-ads.txt from the root of the developer-website host; a github.io/Eddie-G/ path won't work.
Use a dedicated support address, not your personal email.
MS Store, Epic and portals all ask for a privacy policy URL.
doneMessage: Every store form asking for a website, privacy URL or support contact can now be answered.

title: Prepare legal name, bank account and tax ID
statusNote: No store accounts or payout details exist yet; every PC store asks for the same data.
cost: $0 (an EIN is free from the IRS)
steps: Choose: sell as an individual (SSN) or sole proprietor/LLC (EIN).
Optional: get a free EIN at irs.gov so your SSN isn't on store tax forms.
Have a bank account in exactly your legal name (or the LLC's).
Get a business address and phone you're OK showing EU buyers (DSA trader info).
Keep W-9 details ready; each store runs its own tax interview.
feedback: Steam rejects aliases and DBAs: legal name, tax name and bank name must match.
A newly issued EIN can take up to 30 days to validate in Steam's tax check.
A PO box or virtual office keeps your home address off EU store pages.
doneMessage: You have everything every store's payout and tax forms will ask for.

title: Join Steamworks and pay the $100 Steam Direct fee
statusNote: No Steamworks account yet; the 21-day release wait starts only when the fee is paid.
steps: Use a Steam account with Steam Guard mobile authenticator on.
Go to partner.steamgames.com/steamdirect; enter your legal name and address.
Sign the Steam distribution agreement.
Pay the $100 Steam Direct fee to get the App ID.
Add a phone number: SMS codes are needed to set builds live after release.
feedback: Pay early: the 21-day wait (30 in an older doc revision) counts from payment.
Only an admin of the partner account can pay the fee.
Demos are separate App IDs tied to this game; no extra fee was found in the docs.
doneMessage: You have an App ID; build the store page and depots while verification runs.

title: Finish Steam tax interview, bank and identity checks
statusNote: Needs the Steamworks account first.
steps: Do the tax interview (TaxIdentity by Lilaham) in one sitting; W-9 data for US.
Enter bank routing number, account number and bank address.
Answer any document requests from Valve quickly.
Watch the Steamworks dashboard until it shows verified.
feedback: The interview can't be saved halfway; have your SSN or EIN at hand.
Name mismatches between tax, bank and legal name cause most delays.
doneMessage: Valve can pay you, and release becomes possible once the wait and reviews are done.

title: Create an itch.io account and set up payouts
statusNote: No itch.io account yet.
steps: Sign up at itch.io and verify your email.
Payment settings: pick 'Collected by itch.io, paid later' (handles VAT) or 'Direct to you'.
Complete the tax interview (W-9) to avoid 30% withholding.
Set your revenue share (default 10% to itch; any 0-100%).
feedback: Payment-processor fees (about 2.9% + $0.30) come on top of itch's share.
Payouts can be held for review; don't plan cash flow around launch day.
doneMessage: You can create the itch.io page and take payments.

title: Register a free Microsoft Store individual account
statusNote: No Partner Center account yet.
cost: Free for individuals ($99 one-time for companies)
steps: Sign in to Partner Center with a personal Microsoft account.
Choose Individual developer; verify with government ID and a selfie.
Fill in the tax profile (W-9) and payout account.
Apps and games > New product > MSIX or PWA app; reserve 'Alien Sudoku'.
Copy Package/Identity/Name, Publisher (CN=...) and display name from Product identity.
feedback: Choose MSIX, not EXE/MSI: Microsoft signs MSIX for free and sells it for you.
Use the same publisher name ('Eddie G') as on your other stores.
doneMessage: The name is reserved and you have the identity values the MSIX build needs.

title: Optional: open an Epic Developer Portal org, pay $100
statusNote: No Epic account; lower priority than Steam, itch and Microsoft Store.
steps: Create an Epic account (18+) and an organization of type Individual.
Accept the Epic Games Store Distribution Agreement.
Complete trader verification, the tax interview (W-9) and Hyperwallet payout.
Pay the $100 submission fee for the product.
feedback: You keep 100% of the first $1M net per product per year, then 88%.
Epic First Run (6 months at 100%) needs PC exclusivity; skip it.
Skip Epic for now if time is short; small puzzle games get little traffic there.
doneMessage: You can create the Epic product page and upload builds.

title: Windows x64 Electron build (win-unpacked)
statusNote: game/desktop/out has win-unpacked, the NSIS installer and the portable exe for 1.0.0 (unsigned).
steps: cd game/desktop && npm run dist:win
Use out/win-unpacked as the Steam, Epic and GOG content folder.
Run npm run smoke, and rebuild after every game change before uploading.
feedback: Stores install the unpacked folder; never upload the NSIS installer to Steam, Epic or GOG.
Bump the version in desktop/package.json for each store build.
doneMessage: The Windows build every PC store needs already exists.

title: Add gamepad input, fullscreen flag and Deck fixes
statusNote: Input is mouse, touch and keyboard only, and the window opens at 1280x860, taller than a Deck's 800 px screen.
steps: Add Gamepad API input: D-pad moves; face buttons, bumpers and a picker place glyphs.
Map notes, undo, hint, pause and back to controller buttons.
Show controller button prompts while a pad is used; hide keyboard hints.
Add a --fullscreen switch; start fullscreen when SteamDeck=1 is set.
Check all text is at least 9 px tall at 1280x800; make the name prompt skippable.
feedback: Without controller support the best Deck badge is Playable, likely Unsupported.
Verified needs full controller access, controller glyphs and readable text at 1280x800.
Only tick 'controller support' on the store page once this ships.
doneMessage: The game can earn a Steam Deck badge and plays from the couch.

title: Build a Linux folder build for Steam and itch
statusNote: Linux targets are AppImage and deb only and haven't been built yet; Steam needs a plain folder (dir target).
steps: Add a 'dir' Linux target and set linux.executableName to 'alien-sudoku'.
Run npm run dist:linux in this workspace, then npm run smoke.
Plan the Steam Linux launch option with the --no-sandbox argument.
Test under Steam (Linux PC or Steam Deck) before listing Linux on the store.
feedback: Electron's setuid sandbox fails inside Steam's Linux container; pass --no-sandbox as a launch argument, not in code.
Every OS listed on the page must launch, or build review fails.
Windows-only plus Proton is an acceptable first release.
doneMessage: You have a native Linux build ready for a Steam depot and itch.

title: Write SteamPipe depot scripts and upload steps
statusNote: No Steam App ID or depot IDs exist yet.
steps: Create game/desktop/steam/app_build.vdf with one depot per OS.
Windows content: out/win-unpacked; Linux: out/linux-unpacked.
Set SetLive to a password-protected beta branch, never default.
Document: steamcmd +login <user> +run_app_build <path>/app_build.vdf +quit.
Set launch options: 'Alien Sudoku.exe' (Windows), 'alien-sudoku --no-sandbox' (Linux).
feedback: This workspace can't reach Steam's servers; run steamcmd on your own PC.
'status = 6' usually means a wrong App/depot ID, permissions or ContentRoot.
The default branch is set live in Steamworks (SMS code after release).
doneMessage: Uploading a new Steam build is now one command.

title: macOS: sign and notarize a universal build
statusNote: The mac target has identity null; there's no Mac here and GitHub Actions jobs don't start.
cost: $99/year Apple Developer Program (same account as iOS)
time: Half a day on a Mac
steps: Join the Apple Developer Program (same account as the iOS app).
Create a Developer ID Application certificate.
Remove identity: null; set APPLE_ID, APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD, APPLE_TEAM_ID.
Run npm run dist:mac on a Mac and confirm notarization passed.
In Steamworks tick '64 Bit Binaries Included' and 'App Bundles Are Notarized'.
feedback: Steam requires new macOS apps to be 64-bit and notarized.
Launch without macOS if no Mac is available; add it later as a free update.
Unsigned Mac zips on itch need 'Open Anyway' in Privacy & Security.
doneMessage: Mac players on Steam, itch and GOG can now buy and run the game.

title: Make an embed web zip without the service worker
statusNote: game/dist (56 files, 2.4 MB) exists, but the web build registers a PWA service worker.
steps: Add a build flag (e.g. VITE_TARGET=embed) that skips the service worker and install prompt.
Build, then zip the contents of dist/ so index.html is at the zip root.
Check: at most 1,000 files, 500 MB unpacked, 200 MB per file, 240-char paths.
If the web stays a demo, build a demo variant (e.g. Sector 1 + Daily).
feedback: Saves use the 'alien-sudoku:' localStorage prefix, which avoids clashes on itch's shared game domain.
Keep base './': itch and portals serve games from a sub-folder.
The same zip is the starting point for CrazyGames.
doneMessage: The web build drops cleanly into itch.io and web portals.

title: Build a Store MSIX package with electron-builder
statusNote: There is no appx target, and electron-builder can't build MSIX on Linux, so it needs a Windows 10/11 PC.
steps: Add an 'appx' target with identityName, publisher (CN=...), publisherDisplayName from Partner Center.
Set applicationId 'AlienSudoku', displayName 'Alien Sudoku', languages en-US.
Add tile PNGs in desktop/build/appx (StoreLogo, Square44x44Logo, Square150x150Logo, Wide310x150Logo).
On Windows with the Windows SDK: npm run dist:win.
Install the package locally (Developer Mode) and play a full game.
feedback: Without your own tile images you get placeholder art.
Publisher must match Partner Center exactly or the upload is rejected.
The Store re-signs MSIX, so no code-signing certificate is needed.
doneMessage: You have a Store-ready package that Microsoft signs and updates for you.

title: Optional: code-sign Windows downloads
statusNote: The NSIS and portable exes are unsigned, so direct downloads trigger SmartScreen.
steps: Only needed for itch/website downloads or the Store EXE path; Steam, Epic, GOG and MSIX don't need it.
US individual: sign up for Azure Artifact Signing Basic ($9.99/mo) and pass identity validation.
Configure electron-builder's Azure signing (runs on Windows) or use jsign.
Sign and timestamp the exe and installer; test a download on a clean PC.
feedback: EV certificates no longer skip SmartScreen (since 2024); don't pay extra for EV.
Reputation builds with downloads; early users may still see a warning.
Certificates issued after March 1, 2026 last at most 460 days.
doneMessage: Direct downloads now carry your verified name and earn SmartScreen reputation.

title: Make key art, Steam capsules, library art and icons
statusNote: Only a 1024 px app icon and a 2732 px splash exist in game/assets; no key art or logo lockup.
steps: Make layered key art: aliens, glyph grid, 'Alien Sudoku' logo.
Store: header 920x430, small 462x174, main 1232x706, vertical 748x896.
Library: capsule 600x900, header 920x430, hero 3840x1240 (no text, key art in central 860x380).
Library logo PNG 1280 wide and/or 720 tall, transparent background.
Icons: app icon 184x184 JPG; shortcut icon 256 or 512 PNG/ICO; optional background 1438x810.
feedback: Capsules may only show art, the name and an official subtitle: no review quotes, awards, 'on sale' or calls to action.
The small capsule must read at 120x45: make the logo nearly fill it.
AI-assisted store art belongs in your AI disclosure.
doneMessage: One art set now covers Steam and resizes for itch, Microsoft and Epic.

title: Capture 1920x1080 screenshots and a short trailer
statusNote: docs/ has 3 images at 1990x664 and 1590x1338; none are 16:9 at 1920x1080.
steps: Capture at least 5 gameplay shots at 1920x1080 from the Electron build: campaign, daily, duel, zen, themes.
Mark at least 4 as suitable for all ages in Steamworks.
Record a 30-60 s trailer: 1920x1080, 30 or 60 fps, H.264 + AAC MP4, 5,000+ kbps.
Pick a 1920x1080 frame of the video as the thumbnail.
feedback: Screenshots must be real gameplay, not concept art or marketing text.
Lead with the hook: alien glyphs instead of digits, then the Duel race.
Reuse them for itch, Microsoft (1366x768 or larger), Epic and the press kit.
doneMessage: Your media set is ready for every store page and the press kit.

title: Fill in the Steam store page
statusNote: Listing text drafts exist in docs/STORE_CHECKLIST.md but describe the phone version.
steps: Short description (300 chars max) and long text from STORE_CHECKLIST.md, minus phone and ad wording.
Call the Duel opponent a 'computer rival', not 'AI', to avoid confusion with the AI disclosure.
Genres Casual, Indie; tags Puzzle, Logic, Casual, Relaxing, Sci-fi, Aliens, Space, Singleplayer, Cute.
Language English; features Single-player; Family Sharing on.
System requirements: Windows 10/11 64-bit, 4 GB RAM, 500 MB disk; Linux/macOS only once tested.
Upload capsules, library art, screenshots and the trailer.
feedback: Every listed feature (controller, achievements, Cloud) must exist in the build or review fails.
Don't claim Steam Deck Verified; Valve assigns badges.
doneMessage: The page is ready to send to Valve for review.

title: Answer Steam's content survey and AI disclosure
statusNote: Not started; art, themes, music code and probably some text were AI-assisted, so the AI section applies.
steps: Mature content: No to violence/gore, nudity, sexual content and general mature content.
AI section, Pre-Generated: Yes; paste the disclosure text from pc.md section 2.5.
Live-Generated: No (pre-built puzzles; the Duel rival is a scripted algorithm).
Add store art and in-game text to the disclosure if AI helped make them.
Confirm you hold rights to all content (licensed photos, OFL fonts).
feedback: The disclosure is printed on the store page; plain, specific wording reads best.
The January 2026 survey focuses on player-facing content, not coding tools.
Under-disclosing is a policy risk; over-explaining is not.
doneMessage: Your content survey is complete and honest, one less review blocker.

title: Set Steam price, regional prices and launch discount
statusNote: No PC price decided yet.
steps: Enter the USD base price (e.g. $3.99).
Accept Steam's recommended regional prices.
Optionally set a launch discount (10-20%; max 40%, 7-14 days) before release.
Leave Family Sharing on.
feedback: After launch no discounts for 30 days except the launch discount.
Raising the price later blocks discounts for 30 days.
doneMessage: Pricing is set for every Steam region.

title: Build a press kit page
statusNote: No press page; screenshots and texts are spread across docs/.
steps: Fact sheet: developer, release date, platforms, price, website, contact.
Description, features, trailer, 6-10 screenshots, logo, key art, icon.
Credits (photos, fonts) and a one-line honest AI-assistance note.
One zip with everything; host at /press and link it from Steam and itch.
feedback: Press and curators want one-click downloads and a clear contact.
Send Steam keys to sudoku/puzzle creators along with the press link.
doneMessage: Press, YouTubers and curators can cover the game without asking you for files.

title: Create the itch.io page, cover and AI disclosure

Cover image 630x500 (315:250 ratio; minimum 315x250).
Add 3-5 screenshots, trailer link, description, genre Puzzle, up to 10 tags.

Say on the page that Windows may show SmartScreen for unsigned downloads.

Keep the IARC certificate ID; other IARC stores can reuse it.
Screenshots must fit the rating you get.
doneMessage: The Microsoft listing is ready for a package.

statusNote: No Epic organization yet.

Upload key art, logo and screenshots per the portal's media guide.
Write the description and About blocks (up to 12); set the price.
Optionally publish the product home page early for awareness.

doneMessage: The Epic page is ready for a build.

Push Linux (and Mac) channels only after testing them.

Test the Windows build via Proton on a Steam Deck or Linux PC (and the Linux depot).
Request a few Steam keys for friends to test.
feedback: 'Invalid content configuration' means no build is live on that branch or the launch option is wrong.
Saves live in %APPDATA%/Alien Sudoku and survive updates.
doneMessage: You've seen the real Steam install work, so build review is a formality.

statusNote: No MSIX package exists yet.

Run it against the .appx/.msix and fix any failures.
Install, launch, play and uninstall on a clean Windows 10/11 user.

statusNote: No store page yet.

steps: Complete the store page items in the Steamworks release checklist.
Submit for review at least 7 business days before you want it public.

Keep it public at least 2 weeks before release.

Common fixes: text in capsules, features the build lacks, non-gameplay screenshots.

statusNote: No build uploaded yet.

Submit for build review.

doneMessage: Deck and Steam Machine owners can see how well the game runs.

Check every section is complete and submit.

Content, screenshots and age rating must match.
doneMessage: Certification passed; publish whenever you're ready.

Submit the offer and binary for review.

Use the newest BuildPatchTool version Epic's docs list.

title: Publish the itch.io page
statusNote: No itch project yet.

Post a launch devlog with a link to the Steam page.
Push updates with butler; post a devlog for each.

doneMessage: Alien Sudoku is live and playable on itch.io.

steps: Build a demo (e.g. Sector 1 + Daily) as a separate demo app; pass its build review.
With the base game page public, register before the deadline.
Submit demo + page for review by Valve's date (Jan 18 for press preview).
Release the full game after the fest ends.

February is tight from today; June 2027 is the realistic fest.
doneMessage: Your demo is in front of fest players and wishlists can grow.

title: Release on Steam
statusNote: Nothing on Steam yet.
steps: Confirm: 21 days since paying, 2+ weeks Coming Soon, build reviewed, account verified.

Press Release in Steamworks at your chosen time.
Post a launch announcement and answer early reviews.

Avoid launching in the middle of a big seasonal sale.

statusNote: Not submitted yet.
steps: After certification, press Publish now.
Check the live listing, rating and price.
Ship updates as new MSIX submissions with higher versions.

title: Optional: release on the Epic Games Store
statusNote: Not submitted yet.

statusNote: Starts after release.

Join seasonal sales once 30 days have passed since launch.
Post an update event with every patch.

statusNote: Blocked until GOG accepts the game and sends a contract.

doneMessage: GOG has everything it needs to sell the game DRM-free.

statusNote: The web build fits the limits (2.4 MB) but there's no portal account and a free web version may clash with PC pricing.

statusNote: src/platform/ads.js only drives AdMob on phones; web and desktop have no ads.
steps: Add a portal adapter behind a build flag.
Map interstitial to midgame/commercial break, rewarded to rewarded break.
Mute music and pause input during ads; send gameplay start/stop events.
Use the portal's save/data API if required; keep PC and itch ad-free.

Reuse the existing 'between games' and 'extra hint/second chance' moments.
doneMessage: A portal build can earn ad revenue without touching the PC version.

title: Optional: apply to Poki (web-exclusive deal)
statusNote: Not applied; Poki's program is closed beta and prefers web exclusivity.
time: 1 hour to apply; weeks to hear back
steps: Read Poki's deal types; Web Exclusive is the default.
